svg.title: Allocate Startup Capital Before Expanding the Rights Portfolio
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-buckets; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Startup Capital Before Expanding the Rights Portfolio; subtitle: Four buckets illustrate a $100,000 plan within $25,000–$250,000.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are USD allocations for the illustrative $100,000 plan, not annual expenses or canonical revenue. The same 35% / 25% / 20% / 20% split produces $25,000 and $250,000 endpoint comparisons stated in the details. Startup capital does not establish runway: recurring monthly opex is $2,000–$15,000 and first-deal timing is 6–24 months.; caption: The four allocations sum to $100,000. The liquidity bucket covers two months at $10,000 recurring monthly opex, so separately fund the remaining development period and variable costs.; stages: label: Rights diligence and contracting; value: $35,000 central plan allocation for defensible grants; numeric value: 35000.0; detail: Allocate 35% to title investigation, asset schedules, and contract drafting. Endpoint allocations are $8,750 at $25,000 and $87,500 at $250,000.; label: Buyer validation and packaging; value: $25,000 central plan allocation for commercial evidence; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Allocate 25% to technical demonstrations, buyer interviews, and scoped licensing materials. Endpoint allocations are $6,250 at $25,000 and $62,500 at $250,000.; label: Reporting and obligation systems; value: $20,000 central plan allocation for inspectable operations; numeric value: 20000.0; detail: Allocate 20% to report templates, controlled document storage, SQLite reconciliation, and renewal scheduling. Endpoint allocations are $5,000 and $50,000 respectively.; label: Uncommitted operating liquidity; value: $20,000 central plan allocation for cash continuity; numeric value: 20000.0; detail: Hold 20% as cash rather than recording an immediate expense. Endpoint allocations are $5,000 and $50,000; do not treat this reserve as acquisition funding twice.
